content.value_statement: Teams often miss critical test coverage when planning new features or improving legacy systems. This skill turns project context into practical test plans, coverage targets, and quality gates.
actual_capabilities: Defines coverage targets for unit, integration, end-to-end, and performance tests.
Provides templates for test plans and test case documentation.
Maps project risks to testing priorities and quality gates.
Recommends common testing tools for JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python projects.
Includes example patterns for fixtures, factories, mocking, and parameterized tests.
limitations: It does not execute tests or inspect runtime coverage reports by itself.
Tool recommendations may need updates for uncommon frameworks or older stacks.
Generated plans still require domain review from engineers and QA owners.
Performance testing examples need environment-specific targets before use.

use_cases.title: Plan Testing For A New Feature
use_cases.description: Create a test strategy with coverage targets, critical paths, and quality gates before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify missing unit, integration, end-to-end, and performance tests for an existing codebase.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Documentation
use_cases.description: Use structured templates to document test plans, test cases, acceptance criteria, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test plan for this feature: [feature]. Include unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage targets.

prompt_templates.title: Find Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project context: [context]. Identify likely test coverage gaps and recommend prioritized test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design Quality Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design quality gates for this release workflow: [workflow]. Include coverage thresholds, required checks, and failure criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Build Risk-Based Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced strategy for complex or regulated systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a risk-based testing strategy for this system: [system]. Rank risks, define test layers, and propose ownership.

output_examples.input: A checkout feature needs a test plan before development begins.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering payment logic, cart updates, order creation, email confirmation, rollback behavior, and release quality gates.

output_examples.input: An API has low confidence after several production defects.
output_examples.output: A prioritized coverage review with endpoint validation tests, contract tests, database checks, and regression cases for known failure modes.

output_examples.input: A team wants consistent test case documentation.
output_examples.output: A reusable test case format with preconditions, data needs, steps, expected results, edge cases, and traceability notes.

best_practices: Start with business-critical paths, then expand coverage to lower-risk areas.
Use integration tests for interfaces and unit tests for isolated business rules.
Review generated plans with engineers who understand system constraints.
anti_patterns: Do not treat high coverage percentages as proof of quality.
Do not write tests that depend on execution order or shared mutable state.
Do not copy performance targets without adapting them to the real environment.

faq.question: Can this skill choose a testing framework?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common tools and recommends options based on project language, framework, and testing needs.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides strategy, templates, and guidance. Users or agents must run the actual test commands.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prioritize coverage gaps and suggest incremental tests for risky areas first.

faq.question: Does it cover performance testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for load, stress, spike, and soak testing, with practical planning criteria.

faq.question: Is it useful for both frontend and backend teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for UI components, API endpoints, databases, workflows, and service integrations.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
